conflicts.point: Whether labor agencies should mandate continuous operational transparency and demographic auditing rights directly for collective bargaining units before enterprise AI deployment occurs.

positions.stance: Mandatory union inspections and runtime data access operate as an institutional veto that freezes administrative workflows into permanent obsolescence.
Mandating runtime data access and demographic auditing rights under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act achieves structural oversight without erecting bureaucratic entry barriers.

verdicts.conflict: Whether labor agencies should mandate continuous operational transparency and demographic auditing rights directly for collective bargaining units before enterprise AI deployment occurs.
verdicts.rationale: Neither side provides empirical data from enterprise deployments to prove whether mandatory union data access slows innovation or prevents bias. Both positions rely on theoretical projections of administrative obsolescence or worker harm without comparative workplace trials.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Peer-reviewed studies tracking error rates and job retention in firms with mandatory transparency versus those with voluntary rules.
